note: A first listening exercise (home-and-colour:1 and 2): tap a note and then Do to hear home, tap the major and the minor chord that differ by one note, then name major or minor 3rds in the ear game by its buttons (M3, m3) and try it on a song. One staff per step, each showing only the notes that step names; the key is moves (any key), named as {{=key}}, with a {{?key}} line on what stays the same.

exercise.title: Home, and the note that makes major or minor
exercise.why: A tune comes to rest on Do, and the 3rd above Do is the one note that differs between major and minor, so hearing those two notes tells you where home is and what colour it has.

cells.text:
The staff below shows the {{=key}} major scale with its solfège names: tap a note to hear it. Tap {{1}}, then {{7}}, and wait. Then tap {{1}} again to come home.
Try the other notes the same way: tap one, wait, then tap {{1}}.
Practice until you hear {{1}} coming before you tap it.

cells.heading: One note makes major or minor

cells.text: Tap {{1}} {{3}} {{5}} on the staff below: a major chord, one note at a time.

Now tap {{1}} {{b3}} {{5}} on this staff: the minor chord on the same note. Only the middle note moved, down a half step.
Go back and forth between the two staffs. Practice until you can tell them apart with your eyes closed.
{{?key}}In another key the notes are new, and the two chords still differ by that one middle note.

Press Start in the game below to hear two notes together. Pick M3 for a major 3rd, the bottom of a major chord, or m3 for a minor 3rd, the bottom of a minor chord.
Then put on a song you like, and say whether it is major or minor.
